quickStart: For an immediate emergency in Ireland, call 112 or 999.
For public poison advice, call the National Poisons Information Centre on 01 809 2166 from 8am to 10pm. In an emergency call 112 or 999.
For someone to talk to, call Samaritans free on 116 123, day or night.
Review emergency contacts, health information, legal document locations, insurance, bank accounts, pensions, and essential liabilities.
If someone has died, identify the executor or authorised representative and use the current Courts Service, Revenue, HSE, and provider procedures.
Keep the export encrypted. Never put passwords, PINs, MyGovID or Revenue Online Service credentials, authentication codes, or recovery keys in it.

firstActions: Check the PPS number against official records
Keep PPS and card details confidential and share only when a service requires them

Verify phone and email details

legalNotes: This guide is general information, not legal, tax, insurance, or financial advice.
Ireland means the Republic of Ireland; Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom and follows different systems and laws.
PPS numbers are sensitive personal data. The Department of Social Protection says a PPS number has 7 digits followed by one or two letters; share it only with authorised bodies when needed.
Medical cards and GP visit cards have their own HSE eligibility requirements; do not assume every resident is entitled to a card or identical public coverage.
The Courts Service explains that probate or administration may be required. Revenue forms and tax steps depend on the date of death and estate facts.
Ireland has Capital Acquisitions Tax (CAT) on gifts and inheritances; tax thresholds, reliefs, filing, and payment depend on the facts and current Revenue rules.
An enduring power of attorney and advance healthcare directive are separate Decision Support Service arrangements. Confirm registration, activation, and authority before relying on a document.
Public-service guidance: practical arrangements after a death: https://www.citizensinformation.ie/en/death/practical-arrangements-after-a-death/
Decision Support Service: enduring power of attorney: https://www.decisionsupportservice.ie/services/enduring-power-attorney-epa
Decision Support Service: advance healthcare directives: https://www.decisionsupportservice.ie/services/advance-healthcare-directives

fileStructure: The export ZIP may contain a spreadsheet, PDFs, and this access guide.
Treat every file as sensitive; it may include identity, health, financial, and legal references.
dataAccess: Extract to a private, encrypted location and keep an untouched backup.
Share only with trusted authorised people; a family relationship alone does not grant legal access.
Store credentials in a reputable password manager with an emergency-access feature, not in this export.
securityTips: Never put passwords, PINs, PPS portal credentials, authentication codes, or recovery keys in the export.
Use encrypted storage and secure channels for sensitive documents.
Review after major life events and at least annually; remove outdated copies securely.

recoveryRoadmap.description: A general checklist after a death in Ireland. Confirm the representative's authority and current legal, tax, and provider requirements before acting.

meta.title: Family Recovery Roadmap - Ireland
meta.reviewedBy: Government and public-service sources reviewed; case-specific legal and tax advice may be needed

intro.condolence: We are sorry for your loss. This checklist is intended to make the first practical steps clearer.
intro.howToUse: Register the death, identify the executor or administrator, notify relevant agencies and providers, and keep a record of each action.

startHere: Register the death and obtain the records requested by the relevant organisations.
Locate the will and identify the executor; confirm whether a grant of representation is required.
Contact Revenue, the Department of Social Protection, banks, insurers, employers, pension providers, and utilities as appropriate.
List assets, debts, regular payments, and claims; confirm responsibility before changing payments or distributing property.
Keep a log of contacts, forms, and documents supplied. Do not use the deceased person's online credentials or accounts without authority.
legalFramework: Courts Service probate and grant-of-representation procedures.
Revenue income tax, CAT, probate-related forms, and estate obligations.
Decision Support Service enduring powers of attorney and advance healthcare directives.
State pensions, occupational pension scheme rules, insurance contracts, and beneficiary nominations.

phases.title: Register and establish authority
phases.focus: Follow official registration guidance, locate the will, and identify who may act.

keyActions.action: Register the death and obtain the death certificate or records required by providers.
keyActions.why: Registration and certificate requirements are needed for later administration.

keyActions.action: Find the will and confirm the executor; contact a solicitor if there is no will, a dispute, or a complex asset situation.
keyActions.why: The executor or administrator must establish authority and may need a grant before dealing with assets.

mustHaveDocuments: Bank, pension, insurance, property, and liability references
criticalMistakes: Assuming next of kin automatically has authority
Putting passwords or authentication codes in an exported record

phases.title: Notify and identify claims
phases.focus: Notify public bodies and providers, and keep an accurate asset and liability inventory.

keyActions.action: Notify Revenue and the Department of Social Protection using current procedures and establish who is authorised to communicate with them.
keyActions.why: Tax, pension, and social welfare records may need to be updated; the information an agency can provide depends on authority.

keyActions.action: Contact banks, insurers, employers, pension providers, lenders, and utilities separately.
keyActions.why: No single government notification completes all private account and benefit processes.

mustHaveDocuments: List of regular bills and liabilities
criticalMistakes: Assuming an asset passes outside the estate

phases.title: Administer and finalise
phases.focus: Complete required court, Revenue, property, and provider steps before final distribution.

keyActions.action: Confirm whether a grant of probate or administration is needed and follow the Courts Service process when required.
keyActions.why: Requirements depend on the will, estate, assets, and institutions involved.

keyActions.action: Check the deceased person's tax obligations and any CAT or estate-related filings with Revenue or a qualified tax adviser.
keyActions.why: The required forms and tax treatment depend on the date of death, recipients, assets, and current law.

criticalMistakes: Distributing assets before confirming legal authority and tax duties
Assuming no CAT or income-tax steps apply
Using the deceased person's digital credentials

phases.title: Review family arrangements
phases.focus: Review the surviving household's estate, pension, insurance, and secure information arrangements.

keyActions.action: Review wills, DSS arrangements, pension nominations, insurance, and emergency contacts with appropriate professionals.
keyActions.why: Major life changes can make current appointments or nominations unsuitable.

keyActions.action: Keep an asset and digital-account index; store credentials only in a suitable password manager.
keyActions.why: A secure index helps authorised people locate records without exposing secrets.

criticalMistakes: Storing credentials in a spreadsheet or PDF

probate.note: A grant of representation may be needed; check the Courts Service and current Revenue requirements.

cat.note: Revenue provides current CAT rules, thresholds, forms, and reliefs. Do not rely on a static amount in this guide.

glossary.definition: A court grant authorising an executor or administrator to deal with an estate; the grant type and whether one is required depend on the case.
Irish tax that may apply to gifts or inheritances. Liability, thresholds, reliefs, and filing duties depend on circumstances and current Revenue rules.
A Decision Support Service arrangement that can authorise a trusted person to act on certain decisions if the donor loses capacity, subject to registration and legal requirements.
